nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants and in-frame deletions alter conserved residues of lamin B1. Lys33 (p.Lys33Glu, p.Lys33del) lies at the intradimer interface of coil 1A and Arg90 (p.Arg90Pro) at the interdimer interface of coil 1B of the alpha-helical rod; other reported variants lie in the N-terminal head domain. Substitution or deletion of these residues is predicted to interfere with dimer or filament assembly, and the corresponding Lys deletion disrupts protofilament assembly of the ancestral C. elegans lamin. The variants are proposed to act dominantly on assembly of the lamin B1 filament of the nuclear lamina rather than by haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: LMNB1 Lys33 and LMNB2 Asn54 lie at the intradimer interface of coil 1A, LMNB1 Arg90 is at the interdimer interface of coil 1B, and LMNB2 Glu398 is at the intradimer interface of coil 2B. Substitution or deletion of these residues would therefore likely interfere with dimer or filament assembly.

genetic_context.description: Missense variants and in-frame deletions at specific residues, with no truncating variants, led both reporting groups to favor a dominant mechanism (dominant negative, with gain of function not excluded) over haploinsufficiency; heterozygous Lmnb1 knockout mice do not have microcephaly. This is an inference from the variant spectrum, structural modeling and overexpression assays, not a measured effect on endogenous lamin B1 in neural cells.

nodes.description: B-type lamins associate with the mitotic spindle, and mice lacking B-type lamins show defects in spindle orientation in neural progenitor cells. One reporting group proposes this as the mechanism of LMNB1/LMNB2 microcephaly, in line with the spindle defects of other primary microcephaly genes. The evidence comes from null mice, not from the heterozygous human variants.

nodes.description: In cells, the variant lamin B1 proteins form an abnormal nuclear lamina. Head-domain variants reduce nuclear localization of lamin B1 and increase the frequency of misshapen nuclei; a coil-region variant increases the frequency of condensed nuclei and lowers steady-state lamin B1 levels in patient lymphoblastoid cells. Overexpressed GFP-tagged variants form nuclear aggregates. The effect has not been shown in patient neural cells.

nodes.description: In lamin B1-deficient mouse embryos, neurons migrating through the cortical plate show nuclear membrane ruptures accompanied by DNA damage and cell death; non-migrating cells in the ventricular zone do not, and constrictive forces provoke the ruptures in cultured Lmnb1-/- neurons. One reporting group proposes, by analogy to the equivalent LMNA variant producing fragile nuclei, that the human LMNB1 variants make neural precursor nuclei mechanically fragile in the same way. Not shown with the human variants.
